questions.question: Hepatitis C virus therapy is an evolving field in which two drugs were recently approved by Health Canada. For simeprevir and sofosbuvir, give the mechanism of action and the genotype(s) susceptible to its use.
questions.question_raw: 39. Hepatitis C virus therapy is an evolving field in which 2 drugs were recently approved by Health Canada. Fill the following table. Drug | Mechanism of action | Genotype(s) susceptible to its use; Simeprevir | | ; Sofosbuvir | |

parts.text: Fill the table for simeprevir and sofosbuvir: mechanism of action and genotype(s) susceptible.

parts_raw.text: Fill the table for Simeprevir and Sofosbuvir: mechanism of action and genotype(s) susceptible

questions.model_answer: Simeprevir - NS3/4A serine protease inhibitor (first-generation); approved for genotype 1 infection (used with an NS5B polymerase inhibitor such as sofosbuvir). Sofosbuvir - NS5B nucleotide polymerase inhibitor (RNA chain-terminator prodrug) with broad pangenotypic activity (genotypes 1-6); used as a component of fixed-dose combination regimens.
questions.cohort_conflict: Cohort limits sofosbuvir to genotypes 1-4; the text states sofosbuvir has broad pangenotypic (1-6) activity.

cohort_answer.text: Simeprevir - NS3a/4a inhibitor - Genotype 1. Sofosbuvir - RNA polymerase inhibitor - Genotypes 1,2,3,4. Additional: NS5B=RNA dependent RNA polymerase, Polymerase inhibitors (Sofosbuvir, Dasabuvir); NS5A=Viral replication/assembly, NS5A inhibitors (Daclatasvir, Ledipasvir, Ombitasvir); NS3=Serine Protease, Protease inhibitors (Telaprevir, Boceprevir, Simeprevir, Paritaprevir).

questions.question: A woman has hepatitis B in pregnancy at 14 weeks.

parts.text: What non-serological test will help you determine if treatment is warranted?
For a table of every possible HBV drug, name one test required to follow adverse effects of each.

parts_raw.text: What non-serological test will help you determine if treatment is warranted.
HBV table with every drug possible and must name one test required to follow adverse effects.

questions.model_answer:
a) HBV DNA (viral load) by PCR.
b) Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF, category B) first line; lamivudine or telbivudine are alternatives.
c) Third trimester (~28–32 weeks) when HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL, to prevent mother-to-child transmission.
d) (1) Tenofovir DF/AF – serum creatinine/renal function and bone mineral density. (2) Adefovir – serum creatinine/renal function. (3) Entecavir – HBV DNA/ALT (check HIV status before starting). (4) Lamivudine – ALT/HBV DNA. (5) Telbivudine – creatine kinase (myopathy). (6) PEG-IFN-α – CBC (leukopenia/thrombocytopenia) and TSH (thyroid autoantibodies).
questions.beyond_mandell: Telbivudine CK monitoring for myopathy is drug-label/guideline based; Mandell does not specify a monitoring test for telbivudine.

cohort_answer.text: Non-serological test: Hep B DNA/viral load; ALT. Treatment: First line: tenofovir; Second line: telbivudine or lamivudine; then monitor ALT every 3-6 months following discontinuation of antivirals, if normal and no active disease, just follow up clinically. When started: If HepBeAg negative - for prevention of mother-child transmission, start in 3rd trimester (28-32wks GA) with VL >200,000 regardless of eAg/ALT, can d/c at delivery (only if reason for starting is VL>200,000 and asymptomatic) or 4 weeks post partum; if HBeAg positive, treat same as non-pregnant females. Drug/monitoring table: TDF - Cr and bone density; Entecavir - LFTs; 3TC - lactic acidosis, CBC; Telbivudine - CPK (low barrier to resistance, good for pregnancy); Interferon gamma - TSH (hypothyroid)

questions.question: For the HBV antiviral agents adefovir, tenofovir, entecavir, lamivudine, telbivudine, and PEG-IFN, name side effects and one laboratory test to monitor for each.
questions.question_raw: Table of antivirals for HBV treatment. Name one laboratory test to monitor for each: Adefovir, Tenofovir, Entecavir, Lamivudine, Telbivudine, PEG-INF

parts.text: Name side effects and monitoring test for each drug.

parts_raw.text: Name side effects and monitoring test for each drug

questions.model_answer: (1) Adefovir – nephrotoxicity; monitor serum creatinine/renal function. (2) Tenofovir DF – renal insufficiency (rising creatinine) and decreased bone mineral density; monitor renal function and bone mineral density. (3) Entecavir – generally well tolerated (headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea; can select HIV M184V); monitor HBV DNA/ALT and check HIV status before starting. (4) Lamivudine – well tolerated, main issue is resistance; monitor ALT/HBV DNA. (5) Telbivudine – myopathy; monitor creatine kinase. (6) PEG-IFN-α – flulike illness, leukopenia/thrombocytopenia, mood/depression, hair loss, thyroid autoantibodies; monitor CBC and TSH.
questions.beyond_mandell: Telbivudine CK monitoring for myopathy is drug-label based; not specified in this Mandell chapter (which notes telbivudine's issue as resistance).

cohort_answer.text: Adefovir: SE lactic acidosis/hepatic steatosis, renal exacerbation, hematuria; monitor ALT, Cr, PO4, lactate/CO2, U/A (avoid in HIV+). Tenofovir: SE osteomalacia/Fanconi syndrome; monitor electrolytes/PO4, CrCl. Entecavir: SE lactic acidosis, alopecia; monitor lactate/CO2, kidney function. Lamivudine: SE lactic acidosis/hepatic steatosis, pancreatitis, neutropenia, rhabdomyolysis; monitor ALT, AST, CO2/lactate, CBC, CK. Telbivudine: SE myalgias, steatosis, lactic acidosis; monitor CK, CO2, ALT/AST. PEG-INF: SE elevated ALP/ALT, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, hypothyroidism; monitor CBC, TSH, LFT

questions.question: For each hepatitis B drug, name one laboratory monitoring test. PEG-IFN is given as an example (TSH). Complete for adefovir, lamivudine, tenofovir, telbivudine, and entecavir.

parts.text: Name one laboratory monitoring test for each hepatitis B drug (PEG-IFN example: TSH): adefovir, lamivudine, tenofovir, telbivudine, entecavir.

parts_raw.text: Hepatitis B Drugs. Name one laboratory monitoring test for each. Given PEG-IFN as an example (TSH). Complete for: Adefovir, Lamivudine, Tenofovir, Telibuvidine, Entecavir.

questions.model_answer: Adefovir: serum creatinine (nephrotoxicity). Lamivudine: serum creatinine (renal dose adjustment for CrCl <50). Tenofovir (TDF): serum creatinine and bone mineral density (follow renal function/BMD). Telbivudine: creatine kinase (CK, for myopathy). Entecavir: HIV serology before initiation (avoids selecting the M184V resistance mutation) plus renal function.
questions.beyond_mandell: Telbivudine CK/myopathy monitoring is standard product/pharmacology guidance, not stated in this chapter; Mandell supports renal monitoring for adefovir/lamivudine/tenofovir and pre-treatment HIV testing for entecavir.

questions.question: For each of the following hepatitis B drugs, name one laboratory monitoring test (PEG-IFN is given as the example: TSH). Drugs: Adefovir, Lamivudine, Tenofovir, Telbivudine, Entecavir.
questions.question_raw: Q25 (2016 PM). Hepatitis B Drugs - Name one lab monitoring test for each. Given PEG-IFN as an example. Drugs: Adefovir, Lamivudine, Tenofovir, Telbivudine, Entecavir

parts.text: Name one lab monitoring test for each drug

parts_raw.text: Name one lab monitoring test for each drug

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Adefovir – serum creatinine/renal function (nephrotoxicity, proximal tubular injury, like tenofovir). (2) Lamivudine – ALT/aminotransferases (monitor for post-treatment flares, >500 IU/mL in ~15% after cessation). (3) Tenofovir (TDF) – serum creatinine/eGFR (proximal tubular injury; bone density a secondary concern). (4) Telbivudine – creatine kinase (CK) (asymptomatic CK elevation in 13%, myopathy). (5) Entecavir – ALT/aminotransferases (plus lactate given the nucleoside-analogue lactic-acidosis black-box warning). Transaminases can be followed for all agents to detect acute flares.

cohort_answer.text: PEG-IFN | TSH. Adefovir | Creatinine, lactate. Lamivudine | Amylase (rare pancreatitis). Tenofovir | Creatinine. Telbivudine | CK. Entecavir | Lactate (if clinical concern), transaminases. (Transaminases can be used for all to monitor acute flare.)

questions.question: Boceprevir and telaprevir.

parts.text: What is the mechanism of action
What two drugs are they used with for treatment of HCV

parts_raw.text: What 2 drugs are they used with for tx of HCV

questions.model_answer: a) First-generation orally administered ketoamide peptidomimetic inhibitors of the HCV NS3 (NS3/4A) serine protease, blocking proteolytic cleavage of the HCV polyprotein; highly prone to resistance when used as monotherapy. b) (1) Pegylated interferon (PEG IFN) and (2) ribavirin (RBV). c) HCV genotype 1. (Both are no longer recommended as therapy, having been supplanted by newer DAAs.)

cohort_answer.text: MOA: All '-previr' target the NS3/4a serine protease; Boceprevir/Telaprevir inhibit HCV protease by forming reversible covalent bond with NS3 serine active site, preventing proteolytic cleavage of HCV polyprotein into NS4B/NS4A/NS5A/NS5B. Used with: PEG IFN (JAK-STAT immunomodulation) and Ribavirin (inhibits viral polymerase, induces mutagenesis). Genotype: HCV genotype 1 (1b > 1a). (No longer recommended per current guidelines due to newer therapies.)
